scenes.t: Thirty-four.
That's how many times, on the record, Donald Trump said the Iran war would end soon.

v.sub: TIMES HE SAID THE WAR WOULD END SOON

scenes.t: Or that it was almost over. Or that a deal to end it was days away.
We went through eight months of speeches, interviews and posts.
We counted every one we could prove, with the date and the source.
Then we checked something else.
What bitcoin and oil actually did, on every one of those days.
The answer surprised us.
Here's every kind of promise, in his own words.
March first. "We intended four to five weeks."

v.said: We intended four to five weeks.

scenes.t: March ninth. "Soon. Very soon."

v.said: Soon. Very soon.

scenes.t: March seventeenth. "We'll be leaving in pretty much the very near future."

v.said: We'll be leaving in pretty much the very near future.

scenes.t: March thirty-first. "Two or three weeks."

v.said: Two or three weeks.

scenes.t: April sixteenth. "It should be ending pretty soon."

v.said: It should be ending pretty soon.

scenes.t: June ninth. "Two or three days."

v.said: Two or three days.

scenes.t: June eleventh. "Over the next few days."

v.said: Over the next few days.

scenes.t: September ninth. "This war will end immediately after our election."

v.said: This war will end immediately after our election.

scenes.t: October ninth. "One way or another, it's gonna be over soon."

v.said: One way or another, it's gonna be over soon.

scenes.t: October thirtieth. "It's going to get wrapped up soon."

v.said: It's going to get wrapped up soon.

scenes.t: November first. "We'll put it away very soon."

v.said: We'll put it away very soon.

scenes.t: And that same night: "It's going to be over very soon. Very soon."

v.said: It's going to be over very soon. Very soon.

scenes.t: Thirty-four times. Here's what happened in between.
Chapter one. Four to five weeks.
February twenty-eighth, twenty twenty-six. American and Israeli strikes hit Iran.

v.head: US and Israeli strikes hit Iran

scenes.t: Iran answers by closing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel that about a fifth of the world's oil passes through.

v.label: STRAIT OF HORMUZ
v.sub: ~1/5 of the world's oil passes here

scenes.t: The day before the war, US oil closed at sixty-seven dollars a barrel.

v.title: US OIL (WTI) · DAY BEFORE THE WAR

scenes.t: Bitcoin closed near sixty-five thousand nine hundred.
The next day, Trump gives his first timeline. "We intended four to five weeks."

v.said: We intended four to five weeks.

scenes.t: Oil doesn't wait. By March sixth, it's at ninety-one dollars.
March ninth. Trump says the end is coming. "Soon, very soon."

v.said: Soon, very soon.

scenes.t: That day, bitcoin jumps almost four percent.
The next day, oil drops from ninety-five dollars to eighty-four.
For a moment, the words work.
But the war keeps going.
March thirteenth. "I don't think it's gonna be long."

v.said: I don't think it's gonna be long.

scenes.t: March twenty-sixth. "Four to six weeks. We're way ahead of schedule."

v.said: Four to six weeks. We're way ahead of schedule.

scenes.t: March thirty-first. "Two or three weeks."

v.said: Two or three weeks.

scenes.t: By then, oil is above one hundred dollars.
April first, in an address to the nation, he promises to finish the job "shortly, very shortly."

v.said: Shortly, very shortly.

scenes.t: April seventh. Oil hits its highest price of the whole war. One hundred fourteen dollars.
That night comes a two-week ceasefire.
Bitcoin jumps two point six percent in one hour, to seventy-two thousand three hundred.
The next day, oil falls sixteen percent.
Trump calls it "Total and complete victory. One hundred percent."

v.said: Total and complete victory. 100%.

scenes.t: Five weeks had passed. The war had not ended.
Chapter two. Days away.
The ceasefire mostly held.
But talks in Islamabad failed, and on April thirteenth, a US naval blockade of Iran's ports took effect.
On April twenty-first, the ceasefire was extended, with no end date.

v.head: Ceasefire extended with no end date

scenes.t: In May, the US struck Iran twice more, and called it "self-defense."
And the deal was always almost done.
May twenty-third. Details "will be announced shortly."

v.said: Details will be announced shortly.

scenes.t: June first. An agreement, "over the next week."

v.said: An agreement over the next week.

scenes.t: June ninth. Signing "could be in two or three days."

v.said: Upon signing, which could be in two or three days.

scenes.t: Bitcoin didn't wait for it. From May thirty-first to June second, it fell more than nine percent.
By June thirtieth, it was at fifty-eight thousand five hundred.
June seventeenth. Finally, a signed paper. The Islamabad Memorandum, with sixty days to negotiate.
The next day, the US ended the blockade, and Hormuz reopened.
By early July, oil had slid below seventy dollars.
For three weeks, it looked over.
Chapter three. "I think it's over."
July eighth. Iran attacks three ships in Hormuz.
The US strikes more than eighty targets.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they hit eighty-five US military sites in Bahrain and Kuwait.

v.sub: US SITES IRAN SAYS IT HIT (BAHRAIN, KUWAIT)

scenes.t: Trump, at the NATO summit. "I think it's over. I don't want to deal with them any more."

v.said: I think it's over. I don't want to deal with them any more.

scenes.t: This time, "over" meant the ceasefire.

v.head: Trump says ceasefire over after US, Iran trade attacks

scenes.t: Bitcoin fell about two and a half percent, to around sixty-two thousand.
July thirteenth. Trump says the blockade is coming back, with a toll on ships.

v.head: Trump says the U.S. will reinstate its blockade on Iran and charge a toll on ships

scenes.t: In two trading days, Brent crude jumps eleven percent.

v.sub: BRENT CRUDE IN TWO TRADING DAYS

scenes.t: August sixth, in the Oval Office. "I don't think they can go much longer."

v.said: I don't think they can go much longer.

scenes.t: By late August, the war is six months old.
It has cost the US more than thirty-seven and a half billion dollars.

v.sub: COST TO THE US BY LATE AUGUST (AP)

scenes.t: Before the war, about one hundred thirty ships a day crossed Hormuz. On August twenty-sixth, twenty-four did.
Then the tone changes.
He's "not in a hurry" to get Iran back to the table.

v.head: Trump used to say he saw a quick end to his Iran war, but 6 months later he claims he's in no hurry

scenes.t: He posts. "Mission accomplished. Twenty twenty-six."
Chapter four. After the election.
September ninth, at Joint Base Andrews. "This war will end immediately after our election."

v.said: This war will end immediately after our election.

scenes.t: That week, US oil crossed one hundred dollars again.
Three days later, in Ireland. "I think it'll be right after the midterms, actually."

v.said: I think it'll be right after the midterms, actually.

scenes.t: "And oil will come tumbling down when that happens."

v.said: And oil will come tumbling down when that happens.

scenes.t: October second, at a rally in Mobile, Alabama. "It's going to end very soon, and probably right after the midterms."

v.said: It's going to end very soon and probably right after the midterms.

scenes.t: October eighth, on Truth Social. The blockade stays.

v.text: …the Blockade will remain in full force and effect…

scenes.t: But "we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections."

v.text: …we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections…

scenes.t: October ninth. "One way or another, it's gonna be over soon."

v.said: One way or another it's gonna be over soon.

scenes.t: October thirtieth. "It's going to get wrapped up soon."

v.said: It's going to get wrapped up soon.

scenes.t: November first. Before a rally in Iowa. "We'll put it away very soon, one way or the other."

v.said: We'll put it away very soon, one way or the other.
v.where: RSBN interview, before the Iowa rally

scenes.t: On stage that night. "It's going to be over very soon. Very soon."

v.said: It's going to be over very soon. Very soon.

scenes.t: And. "At some point, we're going to have to give them the hammer."

v.said: At some point, we're going to have to give them the hammer.

scenes.t: By the end of October, the Pentagon counted twenty-three American service members killed in the war.
Oil was up about seventy percent from a year earlier.
Chapter five. Did the market believe him?
Here's the part we didn't expect.
We lined up all thirty-four statements against the daily prices.
He said it on thirty-one different days.
Bitcoin closed higher on sixteen of them, and lower on fifteen.
That's a coin flip.
Oil? In the trading session on or after his statements, US oil went up nineteen times out of twenty-seven.
The words said "almost over."
The oil price kept saying "not yet."
The biggest moves didn't come from words. They came from events.
The April seventh ceasefire. The June memorandum. The July eighth collapse. The blockade.
From the day before the first strike to November second, bitcoin rose about sixteen percent.
By late October, US oil was up about fifty-four percent.
His side, and the count.
Trump has his own answer.
On October first, he said his "four to six weeks" meant the Iran nuclear threat, which he says he ended "in one night."

v.said: Four to six weeks … meant the nuclear threat, ended "in one night."

scenes.t: Other counts use other rules.
Axios counted twelve signals by March thirtieth.
C N N counted thirty-eight times he said a deal was close, by June ninth.
Our rule. One dated, public statement per place, per day.
All thirty-four sources are in the description.
So what's the lesson for traders?
One. A promise isn't a price.
Bitcoin treated thirty-four "soons" like noise.
Two. Watch what you can measure.
Ships through Hormuz. The blockade. A signed paper. Those moved the market.
Three. When someone says "soon," ask: soon compared to what?
Four to five weeks has now lasted more than eight months.
The midterms were on November third. He said the war would end right after.
Will it end soon this time?

v.big: WILL IT END SOON THIS TIME?
